newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-EU WARNS FIFA ON TRANSFER REGULATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EU WARNS FIFA ON TRANSFER REGULATIONS.

text.p: The European Commission on Friday sent a shot across the bows of football's world governing body, warning that its transfer regulations contravened European Union laws.
The Commission said in a statement that a recent circular by FIFA "constitutes an unjustified obstacle to the free movement of workers".
The FIFA "circular 616" was prompted by a row over Brazilian footballer Ronaldo's status in Europe.
Ronaldo has attempted to buy his way out of a contract with Barcelona of Spain so that he can join Italian side Internazional.
Barcelona have objected to the move, saying transfers must be arranged between clubs and not individuals.
On Monday FIFA said its players' status committee would decide whether the 20-year-old Brazilian was free to move after he paid $27.6 million to free himself from his contract with Barcelona.
FIFA rules state, however, that a player cannot buy out his contract for the purposes of obtaining an international transfer.

The Spanish Football Federation has refused to issue a transfer certificate for Ronaldo on the grounds that such "buyouts" or withdrawal clauses found in Spanish league contracts are valid for domestic transfers only.

The European Commission statement, signed by Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert and Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn said FIFA's circular appeared to maintain a system which had already been ruled illegal by the European Court of Justice and appeared also to contravene EU regulations.
It said they hoped FIFA would "take this preliminary position into account", a signal that the Commission might take the matter further should they not be happy with the outcome.
